# iTOL visualisation and annotation

Nextstrain/Augur performs sequence analysis and phylogenetic inference. iTOL is
used afterward to display and annotate the resulting trees. It is not an upstream
input to Augur, and it does not replace the alignment or tree-inference steps.

## Files generated by the workflow

For HA, `work/HA/itol/` contains:

```text
HA_divergence.nwk
HA_time_years.nwk          # only when source dates pass validation
HA_tip_metadata.tsv
HA_country.txt
HA_clade.txt
export_summary.json
README.md
```

A colour-strip file is generated only when that annotation column has values.
The corresponding NA names begin with `NA_`.

`*_divergence.nwk` preserves the source Auspice cumulative-divergence differences
along branches. Its units are inherited from the source JSON. The driver requests
mutations per site. `*_time_years.nwk` instead stores parent-to-child time intervals
in years. Uploading the latter does not automatically create a correctly labelled
calendar-date axis; configure and check the display in iTOL. The JSON is the source
for absolute node dates and date confidence intervals.

## Using an existing study tree

```bash
python scripts/export_itol.py \
  --auspice raw_data/ha_auspice.json \
  --metadata raw_data/HA/metadata.tsv \
  --outdir work/HA/itol \
  --prefix HA \
  --columns country clade
```

`--metadata` is optional. When supplied, it is authoritative for the tip annotation
fields. Missing observed values remain missing, even if the Auspice file contains
reconstructed values. Without it, the script uses the Auspice node attributes and
records that those attributes can include inferred states. `--no-time-tree` exports
only divergence when node dates are unavailable.

## iTOL steps

1. Open iTOL and upload the desired Newick file.
2. Check the terminal identifiers, root and branch-length scale.
3. Add the generated colour-strip `.txt` datasets to the tree display.
4. Adjust the tree layout, labels, legend and scale bar without changing the
   analysis interpretation. Preserve zero-length branches when they reflect the
   source data.
5. Save the display settings and export the figure in the required format.
   Keep the tree, annotation files and settings together.

The exporter validates unique node identifiers, finite branch-scale values and
parent-child monotonicity. Tiny floating-point negatives within tolerance are
clamped to zero. Invalid divergence values stop the export. Invalid or decreasing
node dates cause temporal Newick export to be omitted, with the reason recorded in
`export_summary.json`; divergence export still proceeds. The source dates are not
altered. A stale temporal file is removed from the destination to prevent reuse.
It exports all terminal tips rather than selecting a study subgroup. Any pruning,
renaming, recolouring or study-specific visual settings applied in iTOL must be
recorded separately. The generated colours are deterministic defaults, not a
reconstruction of every previously published figure setting.

No tree or metadata is uploaded automatically. Review sample identifiers, sensitive
metadata, access settings and applicable data-use permissions before upload.
Clinical and facility annotations are not included in the default export.
